spans.text: The Rozwi Empire expelled Portuguese colonists from the Zimbabwean plateau, but the Ndebele clan of Zulu King MZILIKAZI eventually conquered the area in 1838 during the era of conflict and population displacement known as the Mfecane.

entries.subject: Apportionment Act

spans.text: The 1930 Land Apportionment Act restricted Black land ownership and established rules that would favor the White minority for decades.

A new constitution in 1961 further cemented White minority rule.

In 1965, the government under White Prime Minister Ian SMITH unilaterally declared its independence from the UK.

entries.object: to biracial elections in 1979 and independence (as Zimbabwe) in 1980

spans.text: International diplomacy and an uprising by Black Zimbabweans led to biracial elections in 1979 and independence (as Zimbabwe) in 1980.

entries.description: who led the uprising and became the nation's first prime minister
entries.subject: who
entries.object: the uprising and became the nation's first prime minister

spans.text: Robert MUGABE, who led the uprising and became the nation's first prime minister, was the country's only ruler (as president since 1987) from independence until 2017.

entries.task_id: emmerson mnangagwa|became|president after a military intervention that forced mugabe to resign
entries.description: Emmerson MNANGAGWA became president after a military intervention that forced MUGABE to resign
entries.subject: Emmerson MNANGAGWA
entries.object: president after a military intervention that forced MUGABE to resign

spans.text: In 2017, Vice President Emmerson MNANGAGWA became president after a military intervention that forced MUGABE to resign, and MNANGAGWA cemented power by sidelining rival Grace MUGABE (Robert MUGABE’s wife).

spans.text: In 2017, Vice President Emmerson MNANGAGWA became president after a military intervention that forced MUGABE to resign, and MNANGAGWA cemented power by sidelining rival Grace MUGABE (Robert MUGABE’s wife).
In 2018, MNANGAGWA won the presidential election, and he has maintained the government's longstanding practice of violently disrupting protests and politicizing institutions.
